title: Temporal hotkey fuzz harness for KV/prefix cache under bursty microbursts
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a synthetic load harness that specifically targets temporal hotkey behavior and transient skew to surface regressions in prefix/KV cache hit-rate vs latency vs memory. Unlike steady-state synthetic workloads, this harness will fuzz inter-arrival patterns, token lengths, and prefix churn to mimic realistic microbursts and rapid locality shifts observed in production. The goal is to catch performance degradations that occur only when hotsets shift rapidly or when short-lived high-QPS spikes coincide with suboptimal eviction scheduling.
objectives: Design a repeatable workload generator that mixes Zipfian distribution with time-varying locality windows
Measure tokens/sec and p95 latency against cache hit rate and resident memory under controlled bursts
Detect regressions automatically and create actionable triage artifacts (heatmaps, timeline traces, PR comment summaries)
approach: Workload model: base Zipf alpha configurable (0.6-1.4) + temporal windowing that shifts hotkeys every N seconds (configurable)
Fuzzing knobs: burst magnitude, burst duration, inter-burst slack, token length variance, shard skew multiplier
Execution harness: k8s job that runs driver (go) + agents on test cluster; driver harvests metrics from runtime via tracing endpoints and /metrics export
Data collection: sample per-request latency, tokens emitted, cache hit/miss tags, memory RSS, eviction counts, KV shard contention indicators
Correlation layer: align metrics to 100ms buckets to compute tokens/sec, p95, hit rate, and memory at fine granularity
harness_components: driver: go-based generator with YAML scenario files and random seed control
agent: C shim to emit header tags and measure on-client latency for end-to-end correlation
ingest: narrow Prometheus scrape + high-cardinality trace capture for hotkey samples
analysis: nightly batch that computes baseline EWMA per-metric and stores fingerprints
reporter: auto-post summary to PR/source ticket + attach flamegraph and eviction waterfall
regression_detection_logic: Baseline: keep 14-day rolling EWMA for tokens/sec and p95 during equivalent scenario runs
Trigger: increase in p95 > 20% AND simultaneous drop in hit_rate > 5 percentage points relative to EWMA
Secondary checks: memory increased > 10% with no corresponding hit-rate improvement -> signals leak or thrash
False-positive reduction: require persistent deviation for 3 consecutive scenario runs or a change-point detection p-value < 0.01
On-trigger action: create a regression issue template with attached charts, raw traces (48h window) and suggested blame vectors (eviction policy, kernel scheduling, prefetch)
acceptance_criteria: Harness can replay a configurable scenario and produce deterministic aggregated metrics given the same seed
Nightly run posts a summary artifact to S3 and a digest to #perf-alerts channel
Regression detector has a false-positive rate under manual review of < 15% over 30 trial runs
Generated artifacts include per-bucket heatmap (tokens/sec vs p95), eviction waterfall, and representative trace sample
Run completes within allocated CI time budget (max 90m) when using the small cluster profile
testing_schedule: Week 1: implement generator knobs + minimal driver (Feb 15-Feb 21)
Week 2: integrate metric collection and build reporting (Feb 22-Feb 28)
Week 3: run 30 randomized scenarios, tune thresholds, and evaluate false-positive rate (Mar 1-Mar 7)
Week 4: stabilize harness, add CI job and PR gating (Mar 8-Mar 15)
